title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: Heatwave forecast (38°C)
drivers.evidence: Historical heat events (2025-07, 2025-08) show x1.18 vs baseline; noise-adjusted estimate x1.15. One strong past occurrence, but consistent with seasonal demand. Price increase may dampen, but heat dominates.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 24.9. No events or promotions are scheduled, but a heatwave forecast (38°C) is a known demand driver. Recent weeks show no price or event drivers. The price increase to $13.93 (+4.1%) is notable but not a promotion. Historical data shows heatwaves correlate with demand spikes; in past similar heat events (2025-07, 2025-08), sales averaged x1.18 vs baseline. The noise-adjusted estimate for heat is x1.15. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but that ignores weather. We apply a moderate uplift. Evidence is limited to one prior heatwave with similar intensity. No post-promo dip observed. The median multiplier is adjusted upward with moderate confidence.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 24.9 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 62.7 | 10%-90%: 2.9 - 43.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
